pairs.question: What happens to my body right after I quit smoking?
pairs.answer: As soon as you quit, your body begins to repair the damage caused by smoking. It's amazing how quickly your health can start to improve!
pairs.evidence: As soon as you quit, your body begins to repair the damage caused by smoking.

pairs.question: Is it common for people to struggle with quitting smoking?
pairs.answer: Yes, most people who smoke and use other tobacco products know they should quit but also know it's not easy. You're not alone in this struggle.
pairs.evidence: Most people who smoke and use other tobacco products such as e-cigarettes and vaping devices, know that using is bad for their health and harmful to those around them. They know they should quit but they also know it's not easy.

pairs.question: How many times do people usually try to quit smoking?
pairs.answer: Most people who use have tried to quit before. It's a common part of the quitting journey.
pairs.evidence: Most people who use have tried to quit before.

pairs.question: What can help me quit smoking for good?
pairs.answer: There are lots of proven tools, tips, and support available to help you end your addiction to tobacco. You don't have to do this alone!
pairs.evidence: Fortunately, there's lots of help available. Our proven tools, tips and support can help you end your addiction to tobacco and begin a new, tobacco-free phase of your life.

pairs.question: What should I consider when thinking about quitting?
pairs.answer: It's important to figure out your personal reasons for quitting. Everyone has their own motivation, and understanding yours can help.
pairs.evidence: Every person has their own personal motivation for quitting.

pairs.question: What can I expect after I quit smoking?
pairs.answer: Quitting is a journey, not a single event. There will be challenges, but knowing what to expect can help you prepare.
pairs.evidence: Quitting is a journey, not a single event. Learn what to expect, challenges to prepare for and answers to common questions about quitting.

pairs.question: Are there any tips for successfully quitting smoking?
pairs.answer: Yes! There are top tips that can help you on the path to success. Finding the right strategies can make a big difference.
pairs.evidence: What's the secret to quitting? These top tips can help you on the path to success.

pairs.question: Who can help me quit smoking?
pairs.answer: Your doctor, nurse practitioner, physician assistant, dentist, or other healthcare provider can help you quit smoking. They can provide information and support you need to live tobacco-free.
pairs.evidence: Your doctor, nurse practitioner, physician assistant, dentist or other healthcare provider are key resources for quitting. They can help you discover what medication will work best for you and put you in contact with local resources and your local quitline.

pairs.question: What kind of support can I expect from healthcare providers?
pairs.answer: Healthcare providers can help you craft your own quit plan and offer methods to prevent slip-ups. They often stick with you throughout your quit journey by scheduling follow-up visits or phone calls.
pairs.evidence: They may help you craft your own quit plan, offer methods to prevent slip-ups, or walk through the pros and cons of nixing nicotine. Doctors or healthcare providers often stick with you throughout your quit journey by scheduling follow up visits or phone calls.

pairs.question: Are healthcare professionals judgmental when I try to quit?
pairs.answer: No, healthcare professionals are not there to judge—they're there to help you in any way you need to achieve a tobacco-free life. You can feel comfortable reaching out to them.
pairs.evidence: Remember, healthcare professionals are not there to judge—they're there to help you in any way you need to achieve a tobacco-free life.

pairs.question: Is there a program that can help me quit smoking?
pairs.answer: Yes, hundreds of thousands of people quit smoking through our Freedom From Smoking program. It’s a great resource to consider.
pairs.evidence: Hundreds of thousands of people quit smoking through our Freedom From Smoking program.

pairs.question: What resources are available to help me quit?
pairs.answer: You can view and download tools from the Helping You Quit Resource Library, including a collection of quick reference guides. These can be really helpful during your quit journey.
pairs.evidence: View and download tools to help throughout your quit journey, including a collection of quick reference guides.

pairs.answer: You can make a tax-deductible donation to fund lung disease and lung cancer research, new treatments, and lung health education. Every bit helps!

pairs.question: What should I do if I need help quitting?
pairs.answer: If you need help quitting, reach out to your healthcare provider. They can connect you with local resources and your local quitline.
pairs.evidence: They can help you discover what medication will work best for you and put you in contact with local resources and your local quitline.
